factor_diagnostics.value_notes: California OPC reports the species' geographic range bounded broadly by 3-18 °C surface isotherms, with larval thermal tolerance likely more limiting than adult tolerance. Adult archival-tag/laboratory work found thermal preference behavior across 8-22 °C gradients, modified by food availability and starvation; mating waters are commonly 8-17 °C. This supports SST relevance but does not validate one universal 6-15 °C / 8-13 °C catch-suitability curve across larvae and adults.

factor_diagnostics.value_notes: Adult archival tags found most time below 15 m, with repeated migrations into shallower estuary water; WDFW reports adults in less than 10 m during spring mating and deeper than 16 m in fall/winter. California OPC reports intertidal-to-229 m occurrence, with few crabs beyond 91 m. The configured 2-80 m / 4-75 m interval is a broad shelf/estuary screen, not one year-round preference.
